summary.tldr: Changes sentencing rules so a person convicted of abduction, sexual assault and murder of the same victim can face parole ineligibility for 25 to 40 years.
what_it_does: Requires a life sentence without parole eligibility for at least 25 years, and up to 40 years, for a person convicted of abduction, sexual assault and murder of the same victim in the same event or series of events.
Lets the trial judge ask the jury whether it wants to recommend a parole ineligibility period, and if so, how many years the person should serve before release can be considered.

Allows the judge to replace the 25-year parole ineligibility period with a longer period, from more than 25 years to no more than 40 years, after considering the offender, the offences and the circumstances.
Sets out that the judge may consider any jury recommendation when deciding the parole ineligibility period.
who_it_affects: People convicted of abduction, sexual assault and murder
summary.background: It amends section 745 of the Criminal Code and adds new sections about jury recommendations and parole ineligibility.
